name: Facilitation Architecture
description: Forty-eight facilitation exercises in five lifecycle stages, each with the room it needs, the time it takes, the hard it is, what the group leaves with, the steps to run it, and the failure that is waiting.

rules.title: Facilitation Architecture Rules
rules.intro:
The exercises come from public facilitation practice: the design-sprint tradition, Liberating Structures by Henri Lipmanowicz and Keith McCandless, Lean and Scrum lineage, and methods the field has used long enough that no single author is documented. Each card names an origin where one is documented and says plainly where none is.
Every card answers the four questions a facilitator has in the room - how many, how long, how hard, what we leave with - then the steps, then the failure that usually arrives.

skill.name: facilitation
skill.description: Run a workshop exercise that fits the room you actually have: {cards} facilitation methods in five lifecycle stages, each with group size, time, difficulty, deliverable, steps, and the failure it usually hits. Use when choosing an exercise for a session, when a session has gone flat, or when writing an agenda that has to produce a decision.
skill.title: Facilitation Architecture
skill.intro:
This file is the index. The cards live in `resources/`, one file per stage.

Choosing starts from what the room owes: a shared problem before divergence, a spread of options before convergence, a decision before planning, a plan before the room leaves. Read the stage that matches the debt, then the one card that fits the people and the clock.

When two cards fit, take the one whose failure you can recognize in this room. A method's failure mode is what it costs when it half-works, and a facilitator who can name it will see it coming.

Running one without flattening the room: say what the group leaves with, give the silence its timer, and never fill a pause longer than the instruction. The steps are beats, not a script; the fix is the sentence to say when the beat goes wrong.
commonRules: Name the deliverable before anyone starts. A group that does not know what it walks out with will produce a conversation.
Silence is part of the method. Protect it with a timer and do not narrate it.
One exercise, one debt. Do not stack two methods to fix a room that needs a decision.
When the room goes flat, read the failure line before inventing a new intervention.
An inventory-only card's steps are written for this deck from the method's public definition; the card says so. Do not present them as a source script.
skill.footer: Methods are credited to their public originators where one is documented. The card text is written for this deck.
